note.question: Will adding an internal audit system actually prevent socially harmful performance manipulation when shareholders can profit from undetected misconduct?
note.overview: A principal chooses whether and how effectively to audit, designs a limited-liability performance-pay contract, and anticipates an employee's hidden effort and post-failure manipulation choice. The paper solves the sequential moral-hazard game by backward induction and explicitly characterizes subgame-perfect equilibria, with a perfect-Bayesian extension when audit effectiveness is hidden.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The authors solve the sequential contracting game by backward induction. They derive minimum-cost limited-liability contracts for manipulation prevention and inducement, compare the principal's resulting profit across control regimes, and establish parameter thresholds. Model variants introduce stakeholder verification, internal reputational losses, vicarious liability, wage restrictions, and hidden control effectiveness.

components.label: Subgame-perfect equilibrium of the observable-control principal-agent game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Subgame-perfect equilibrium of the observable-control principal-agent game. The agent's manipulation and effort responses are solved first, optimal wages are derived conditional on prevention or inducement, and the principal then chooses internal-control adoption and effectiveness. The paper explicitly contrasts these subgame-perfect equilibria with the perfect Bayesian equilibrium required when mu is unobservable.
